note: Flat key-value store: booleans and integers only. This is also the entire save file. Harness flags are engine-test fixtures, not design flags -- the ~40 real topic flags land with Act content.

flags.note: Thad has said his opening line. Doc 17 v3 beat 3 -- one canonical line, played sincerely, not a choice. The three-option version and the flag's old writer are both void.

The coach has gone. Doc 17 v3.1 restores the driver's tree, and its EXIT option says so in words: 'He climbs aboard. The coach goes. Beat 7.' Beat 7 does not write it -- two writers on the same fact is a race.

Thad has been told to ask the undertaker. Doc 17 v3.1's first PROGRESS option, and the objective the whole opening runs to. Doc 20 rule 3 -- a location appears on the map when heard of, not when visited -- so this is what puts the undertaker's on the map, and the map cannot carry him until something sets it.
Hob is on screen. Doc 17 v3 beat 9 -- renumbered from beat 8 by the act card moving in ahead of it. Now the second strange encounter rather than the first, and it carries no exposition.
Hob has left frame. Doc 17 beat 10, which is an animation finishing rather than anything the player does, so nothing in content can write it and the opening-sequence driver must.

Thad has learned that Ezra Pike, the man his letter of introduction is addressed to, has been dead six years. Gates the letter's second line set per ruling 19a and doc 23. Nothing writes it yet -- the beat that does is in Act I's opening run of puzzles and is not built, so this is declared-and-unwritten on purpose and check-flag-order reports it.

The opening sequence has handed over control -- doc 17 beat 8. Not a design flag: it exists so a save restored mid-game does not replay the opening, and so a player who has already been told the undertaker's name is not told again. The sequence file names it, so the engine hard-codes nothing.
